title: An Atom's Weight
art: 99:7-8 says whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it. The scene shows the earth opening; what each person carried is not shown, because only God knows it.
The atom's weight (mithqal) is the smallest coin the Quraysh used; the coin itself is not shown.
imagePrompt: A bare wide plain seen from above, the earth opening into a long dark seam that widens; along it a few points of light, some warm and steady and some dim, and dust rising where it opens; ink-wash and parchment texture.

beats.say: The Day of the Earthquake. When the earth is shaken with its final earthquake and discharges its burdens, the people depart separated, to be shown the result of their deeds.
Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it. A mustard seed's worth, a grain of dust's worth: nothing is too small to be seen.

verse.en: So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it.
